title: Grateful Dead Live at Salt Palace on 1973-02-28

ai_review.summary: Warm soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1973 show with smoking China Cat > Rider and tight He’s Gone / The Other One jams, despite early muffling and hiss.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised as one of the top shows of ’73, highlighted by an incendiary China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, a monster He’s Gone, and a seamless Truckin’ → The Other One → Eyes of the World → Morning Dew sequence. The soundboard source is warm but grainy, with noticeable hiss, pops and muffled audio in the early part of the set and an incomplete ending after “Eyes”. Overall the musical energy is high and the vocals and instrumental interplay are described as superb.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars for the show, citing standout jams; recording quality is mixed (average ~3) but does not outweigh the strong musical performance.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early tracks (China Cat to The Promised Land) muffled and slightly distorted; hiss, pops and graininess throughout; missing material after “Eyes” and some dead‑air/tuning cuts noted.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Truckin' > The Other One > Eyes of the World > Morning Dew
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑1973 set list with a strong first set and a second set that flows seamlessly through extended jams; transitions are praised as tight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as excellent; Jerry’s singing is in prime form.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as powerful (“blow‑torching” Jack Straw) and Phil’s vocals highlighted as strong.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s vocal contributions praised, part of the tight harmonies.
